note: Acceptance criteria written BEFORE drafting the skills, per the project brief. Assertions are graded against the agent's produced answer/artifacts. Every assertion is objectively checkable against the research dossiers and the machine-extracted OpenAPI corpus in research/spec-inventory/.

evals.name: nsx-dfw-rule-91
evals.prompt: We're on VCF 9.1. I need to block RDP (tcp/3389) from our app-tier group to our db-tier group in NSX. Both groups already exist. Give me the exact API calls including how to authenticate.
evals.expected_output: Correct Policy API path, correct NSX session auth with both cookie and XSRF header, security-policy-then-rule ordering, prereqs stated, answer explicitly scoped to 9.1.

assertions.text: Uses the Policy API base path /policy/api/v1 for the security policy and rule calls
Does NOT present the Manager API /api/v1 as a valid surface for creating policy objects
Auth uses POST /api/session/create with form fields j_username and j_password
States that BOTH the JSESSIONID cookie AND the X-XSRF-TOKEN header must be sent on subsequent calls
Creates or references a security policy under a domain before creating the rule (correct nesting, not a bare rule POST)
States the prerequisite that both source and destination groups must already exist and be referenced by path
Explicitly labels the answer as applying to VCF 9.1 / NSX 9.1
Includes the caveat that the skill was built from documentation and not validated against a live environment
Contains no endpoint that is absent from the 9.1 nsx_policy_api spec

evals.name: nsx-dfw-rule-90-evidence-asymmetry
evals.prompt: Same thing but we're still on VCF 9.0 — block tcp/3389 between two existing NSX groups. How confident are you in the exact endpoints?
evals.expected_output: Answers for 9.0 while being explicit that NSX 9.0 has no machine-readable OpenAPI spec in the public corpus, so endpoint verification is prose-doc based rather than spec-grade.

assertions.text: Explicitly labels the answer as VCF 9.0 / NSX 9.0
States that no NSX OpenAPI spec is published at the 9.0.0.0 tag of vmware/vcf-api-specs, so 9.0 endpoints are sourced from prose documentation
Does NOT present a 9.1-spec-derived endpoint as verified for 9.0
Still uses the Policy API /policy/api/v1 surface (correct for 9.0 as well)
Answers the confidence question directly rather than deflecting

evals.name: sddc-manager-gone-trap
evals.prompt: In VCF 9.1 SDDC Manager is gone and replaced by VCF Fleet Manager, right? What should I be calling for lifecycle management now?
evals.expected_output: Corrects both halves of the false premise: SDDC Manager still exists (UI deprecated only, API grew), and there is no product named VCF Fleet Manager.

assertions.text: States that SDDC Manager still exists in VCF 9.1 and is in the 9.1 BOM
States that the deprecation is scoped to the SDDC Manager UI, not the API
Does NOT use the name 'VCF Fleet Manager' as a real 9.1 product
Names fleet lifecycle and SDDC lifecycle as the services that replaced the 9.0 standalone Fleet Management Appliance
Notes that the SDDC Manager API surface grew rather than shrank between 9.0 and 9.1
Does not fabricate an endpoint for a 'Fleet Manager' API

evals.name: upgrade-ordering-version-split
evals.prompt: walk me through upgrading our management domain from 9.0 to 9.1 - what order do the components go in and what do i need to check first
evals.expected_output: Correct 9.0->9.1 upgrade sequence with prerequisites, distinguishing this from a 9.0.x maintenance update ordering.

assertions.text: Gives a component ordering rather than a vague 'follow the docs'
Distinguishes the major-version upgrade ordering from the 9.0.x maintenance-update ordering rather than conflating them
States that SDDC Manager itself drives the first half of the 9.0->9.1 upgrade
Calls out prechecks as a prerequisite step
Mentions that workload domains must be at a minimum version before the 9.1 upgrade
Warns that this is a destructive/high-impact operation to verify before execution

evals.name: router-no-version-given
evals.prompt: How do I get an API token so I can start automating against our VCF environment?
evals.expected_output: Resolves the target version before answering rather than defaulting to latest, and distinguishes per-product auth.

assertions.text: Establishes or asks for the target VCF version (9.0 vs 9.1) before committing to an auth flow
Does NOT silently default to 9.1 / 'latest'
Establishes or asks which product the token is for, rather than assuming one API covers VCF
States that SDDC Manager is excluded from VCF SSO and uses its own token flow
If 9.1 is selected, describes the VCF Identity Broker / API client + API token route

evals.name: sddc-manager-token-bash
evals.prompt: write me a bash function that grabs an SDDC Manager API token on VCF 9.0 and refreshes it when it expires. our cert is self-signed for now.
evals.expected_output: Correct token and refresh endpoints, correct payload shapes, correct header, honest handling of the self-signed cert question.

assertions.text: Uses POST /v1/tokens with a JSON body containing username and password
Extracts the accessToken field for the bearer token
Uses the header Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>
Uses refreshToken.id and PATCH /v1/tokens/access-token/refresh for refresh
Notes that the refresh endpoint takes a plain-text refresh token rather than JSON
Addresses the self-signed cert explicitly rather than silently emitting curl -k, and notes that Broadcom docs prescribe replacing certificates rather than disabling verification
Answer is scoped to 9.0 and does not assert 9.1 paths as verified

evals.name: discovery-uncovered-operation
evals.prompt: I need to automate vSAN stretched cluster configuration on VCF 9.1 and I can't find the API anywhere in the docs. How do I find it?
evals.expected_output: Teaches a concrete lookup path instead of guessing an endpoint.

assertions.text: Points to github.com/vmware/vcf-api-specs and names the version tag 9.1.0.0
Gives a concrete way to search the spec corpus (grep/script/jq over the spec files) rather than only saying 'read the docs'
Mentions at least one on-appliance discovery route (e.g. the VCF Operations swagger UI or the NSX openapi spec endpoint)
Does NOT invent a specific vSAN stretched-cluster endpoint and present it as verified
Notes that no on-appliance API-explorer URL pattern is documented for VCF 9.x

evals.name: powercli-module-name-trap
evals.prompt: getting started with powercli against vcf 9.1 - what do i install and how do i connect to sddc manager? i'm on powershell 5.1 on a windows box
evals.expected_output: Correct module name, correct connect cmdlet and its cert flag, and the PowerShell 5.1 deprecation called out.

assertions.text: Names the module VCF.PowerCLI (not VMware.PowerCLI) as the current meta-module
Uses Connect-VcfSddcManagerServer for SDDC Manager
Uses -IgnoreInvalidCertificate for that cmdlet rather than -SkipCertificateCheck
Flags that PowerShell 5.1 is deprecated as of PowerCLI 9.0 and recommends PowerShell 7.x
Does not claim a cmdlet whose existence was not verified in the research

evals.name: prereq-api-client-90-does-not-exist
evals.prompt: I want to set up a service account with a long-lived API token scoped to read-only, so our automation isn't using my personal admin creds. We're on VCF 9.0.
evals.expected_output: Correctly states that SSO-issued, role-scoped API tokens are a 9.1 capability and do not exist in 9.0, then gives the 9.0 route.

assertions.text: States that API clients / API tokens issued by VCF SSO are a 9.1 feature and are NOT available in 9.0
Does NOT walk the user through the 9.1 Fleet Management > Identity & Access > API Clients flow as if it existed in 9.0
Gives the actual 9.0 route: per-product credentials (SDDC Manager /v1/tokens, VCF Operations token/acquire, NSX session, vCenter session)
Mentions NSX principal identities as the documented service-account mechanism for NSX
Notes that VCF built-in roles (VCF Viewer / VCF Administrator) are documented only in the 9.1 doc set

evals.name: prereq-vcenter-90-federated-login-block
evals.prompt: my script authenticates to vcenter with a username and password and creates a session. worked fine on our old 8.x setup, now it fails on the new VCF 9.0 build. what changed?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the 9.0 prerequisite change around non-federated username/password logins rather than generic troubleshooting.

assertions.text: Identifies that vCenter 9.0 blocks non-federated username/password logins as the likely cause
Describes the federated flow (external IdP token exchanged for a session) as the prerequisite that must now be satisfied
Names the vmware-api-session-id header as the session mechanism
Scopes the answer to 9.0 rather than mixing in 9.1 OAuth token support without labelling it
Does not attribute the failure to a certificate problem without evidence

evals.name: prereq-token-death-and-cert-trust
evals.prompt: our VCF 9.1 automation randomly stops working after a few weeks and we have to regenerate credentials. also we keep hitting TLS errors from the python side. what are we doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Surfaces the version-specific prerequisite traps: token TTL ceilings, JIT user inactivity silently killing tokens, and VMCA-signed default certs.

assertions.text: Identifies API Token TTL limits (default 30 days) as a likely cause of the periodic failure
Mentions the JIT user inactivity behaviour, where an inactive user's previously issued API tokens can no longer retrieve access tokens until that user authenticates again
Identifies VMCA-signed default certificates as the cause of the TLS trust errors
Recommends trusting/replacing the CA rather than disabling verification, consistent with Broadcom guidance
Labels these as 9.1 behaviours and does not assert them for 9.0

evals.name: prereq-upgrade-gates
evals.prompt: what has to be true before we can even start the 9.0 to 9.1 upgrade? trying to build a readiness checklist for change control.
evals.expected_output: A genuine version-specific prerequisite checklist, not generic upgrade advice.

assertions.text: States the minimum workload-domain version gate that must be met before the 9.1 upgrade
Includes running prechecks as an explicit gate
Mentions depot / bundle availability (online or offline depot) as a prerequisite
Mentions that OAuth clients are not migrated automatically on the vIDM to identity broker migration and must be manually regenerated
Distinguishes prerequisites that are 9.1-specific from ones that applied in 9.0
Flags items the research could not verify rather than inventing a complete-looking checklist

prerequisite_coverage_rule.rationale: Missing prerequisites is one of the four failure modes the brief names for adversarial review, and prerequisites are where 9.0 and 9.1 diverge most sharply. Treat them structurally, not incidentally.
requirements: Every version-scoped reference file must open with a Prerequisites block before any endpoint is listed.
Each prerequisite is tagged with the version it applies to, and prerequisites that exist in only one version must say so explicitly (e.g. SSO-issued API tokens: 9.1 only).
Each prerequisite states how to verify it is satisfied, not just that it is required.
Where a prerequisite could not be verified in research (e.g. the ports matrix), the block says so rather than omitting it silently.
Adversarial review includes a dedicated pass that asks: for each worked example, what must already be true for this call to succeed, and is that stated?
